Subject: Post-demo — data handling & subprocessor follow-up

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and next steps on the items we discussed related to PII, retention, logging controls, and third-party sharing (telemetry/marketplace flows):

- PII scope: Redwood does not persist customer PII in external telemetry vendors. For hosted customers, request/response payloads may be temporarily cached for routing/ops purposes; we can configure or opt out of request-logging per contract.
- Data retention: Default request/log retention for hosted API is 30 days. We offer configurable retention and SLA-backed options for Dedicated/Private deployments (can be set to 90/180/365 days or disabled).
- Logging controls & audit logs: We maintain request-level audit logs and admin access logs. We can provide sample audit exports and a SOC2 artifacts package.
- Third-party subprocessors: Primary infra — AWS (us-east-1) and GCP (europe-west1 for EU workloads). Telemetry and monitoring: Datadog for metrics/traces, Sentry for error traces (no request bodies). Marketplace billing flows use the cloud marketplace reports and do not push customer raw payloads to external partners.

Attachments: Redwood_Subprocessors_2026Q3.pdf (list of subprocessors + data residency), SOC2_artifacts_link (see Drive link below).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the attached questionnaire (ACME_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx) — I'm happy to fill the sections we typically answer and loop in our security engineer (Vivek) for the technical items.
2) If helpful, we can set a 30-min follow-up with Vivek and Neha to walk through the retention & telemetry controls — propose Wed, Oct 7 at 10:00 AM CET.

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A few clarifying questions from our security team:

1) Can you provide a granular list of subprocessors by function (infrastructure, telemetry, analytics, SSO, billing) and indicate which ones may process customer payloads vs only metadata/metrics?
2) For hosted customers, is request/response payload retention optional? We need a default of 90 days for logs retained for our internal compliance; can that be accommodated or do we need Dedicated/Private?
3) Telemetry vendors: which vendors receive traces/metrics vs error events? Any chance that customer identifiers (user IDs, email hashes) are sent to these vendors?

Jordan — thanks for the detailed questions. See answers below and attached CSV with subprocessor mapping. Vivek (our security/infra lead) and Neha (privacy lead) are CC'd to pick up the questionnaire specifics.

1) Subprocessors by function (summary) — attached redwood_subprocessors_2026Q3.csv (full list):
   - Infrastructure: AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2), GCP (europe-west1) — may host customer workloads and store encrypted data as configured; all infra subprocessors are bound by our DPA.
   - Telemetry/Monitoring: Datadog (metrics + traces), Sentry (error traces, no request bodies), BigQuery (aggregated telemetry for some analytics pipelines) — telemetry ingestion excludes full request payloads in hosted mode; we only send metadata, anonymized ids and sampling traces.
   - Analytics/BI: Looker (aggregated, aggregated-only exports), Segment (metadata routing) — no raw PII exported to analytics by default.
   - Billing/Marketplace: AWS Marketplace reporting flows for purchase/billing; no customer payloads are forwarded to marketplace vendors.

2) Retention: Hosted default is 30 days. We can support 90-day retention as a contract option for hosted customers (may require a small configuration + audit commit). Dedicated/Private gives you full control over retention. We'll note this as a deal-level configuration (DEAL-ACME-2026-08).

3) Telemetry vendor data: Datadog receives metrics and traces (sampling applied). We do NOT send PII or full request bodies to Datadog or Sentry. Any identifiers sent are internal request IDs or hashed/anonymized IDs — we can provide an example telemetry schema.

4) Marketplace flows: Purchasing via AWS Marketplace does not change data flows for payloads. Marketplace reporting provides billing/usage info to AWS for chargeback; payloads remain within Redwood's environment.
